pages.observed: Five samples from 0.0 to 0.8 seconds show a wide pad, closed station and then opening hood leaves. The caption appears in the final two samples.
At 1.0 to 1.8 seconds the hood opens outward, exposing a pale drone on its landing deck. The oilfield equipment stays behind it.
Samples from 2.0 to 2.8 seconds change to a wider pad view. Texas cards appear above the station while the drone starts lifting.
From 3.0 to 3.8 seconds the drone travels upward and right over the open station; its dark ground shadow shifts below it.
At 4.0 to 4.8 seconds the drone continues across the pad. A pin and Permian Basin label appear on the larger Texas card.
The 5.0 to 5.8 second samples show a dotted map connection completed between two pins while the drone travels right over the tank.
The pad remains through 6.4 seconds. At 6.6 seconds a dark tablet stands on a desk beside a visible company-attribution tag.
From 7.0 to 7.8 seconds the tablet fills with a route and three status rows. A blue flag appears above the pressure row in the final sample.
At 8.0 to 8.8 seconds AI alert is visible on the blue flag above Pump pressure. The separate company-attribution tag remains on the desk.
At 9.0 to 9.8 seconds a closer tablet retains the blue alert. The caption changes to the operations-anomaly clause as the attribution tag begins moving.
The company-attribution tag rises across the tablet between 10.0 and 10.8 seconds and approaches the blue alert row.
Across 11.0 to 11.8 seconds the attribution tag hangs beside the blue alert and settles while the route dot changes position.
At 12.2 seconds a letter replaces the tablet. Its generic drone and Air Max label are present as the paper slides left and a stamp enters above.
The stamp moves onto the date area from 13.0 to 13.8 seconds. The latter samples enlarge the letter while the stamp covers most of the date.
From 14.0 to 14.6 seconds the lifted stamp exposes an amber date impression on the letter. Another smaller stamp enters by 14.8 seconds.
At 15.0 to 15.8 seconds a large document view exposes the date, drone and record name. The brown stamp presses over the approval-mark location.
At 16.0 to 16.8 seconds the stamp lifts to the upper right, revealing a check and Approved beside the screening tag while the approval caption remains.
The document stays in the same close view from 17.0 to 17.8 seconds. The named-system caption appears with the drone and Air Max record label already visible.
During 18.0 to 18.8 seconds amber emphasis grows beneath Air Max. The generic drone drawing and approval mark remain together on the letter.
The 19.0 to 19.8 second samples hold the identified generic drone, dated letter and approval mark without another view change.
At 20.0 to 20.8 seconds amber highlighting develops on the screening tag while Approved and the identified drone remain visible beside it.
The completed date, approval and scope hold through 21.6 seconds. At 21.8 seconds the view returns to the airborne drone above equipment.
At 22.0 to 22.8 seconds the drone hovers above the pad. White rings and dashed links appear between the drone and equipment.
The 23.0 to 23.8 second samples retain the hovering drone and route rings. A pale cone extends downward from the camera pod toward the valve.
At 24.2 seconds the drone enlarges in a closer view. Subsequent samples move it right along the dashed connection toward the large ring over a valve.
At 25.0 to 25.8 seconds the drone reaches a white ring over the valve. A dark rectangular inset begins expanding beneath its camera.
The 26.0 to 26.8 second samples show an expanded dark inset with a valve and warm rising shimmer. The drone holds beside it over the tank.
At 27.0 to 27.8 seconds the view changes to a seated person facing a monitor. The valve footage slides onto that screen from the right.
The valve image is loaded by 28.0 seconds. Through 28.8 seconds the seated inspector leans closer with her right hand near the monitor.
At 29.0 to 29.8 seconds the inspector continues facing the loaded screen and raises her stylus hand toward the valve image.
At 30.0 to 30.8 seconds a closer inspector view shows the stylus moving around the warm shimmer as a white dashed oval grows behind its path.
Across 31.0 to 31.8 seconds the oval is complete. A green check appears beside it as the inspector's hand reaches that spot, then the check holds.
At 32.0 to 32.8 seconds the closer view includes the valve vignette. A Follow-up inspection tag appears at the raised finger and begins its arc toward the valve.
At 33.0 to 33.8 seconds the follow-up tag reaches the valve vignette and settles. The inspector's hand moves away while the green confirmation stays on the footage.
At 34.2 seconds the review screen cuts to an upright document holder. The page scrolls upward, bringing the protocol title farther into view.
From 35.0 to 35.8 seconds the title settles near the document center. A small amber mark starts under AI near the end of this page.
At 36.2 seconds the view cuts to a large title detail. AI is highlighted amber at the start of its second line throughout the remaining samples.
Across 37.0 to 37.8 seconds a white tag drops on a short string beneath the highlighted AI and settles with the once-in-a-title text.
At 38.4 seconds the title cuts to a desk tag and calendar. The disclosure explicitly identifies a separate program with no drone.
From 39.0 to 39.8 seconds the large program tag lowers and settles in front of the closed calendar. No inspector or drone appears.
At 40.6 to 40.8 seconds the calendar cover flips up and exposes January 22, 2027 behind the program tag.
The calendar cover moves over its rings and disappears by 41.4 seconds, leaving the January 22, 2027 page fully exposed beside the program tag.
At 42.0 to 42.8 seconds the date and program label remain visible in a closer desk view. An amber bar begins entering from the left near the tag.
The amber Delayed bar reaches the program tag between 43.0 and 43.2 seconds, then stays below its label beside the January calendar.
The January date holds through 44.4 seconds. At 44.6 seconds a wider view retains the delayed program tag and introduces a covered day block.
From 45.0 to 45.8 seconds the day block reveals October 7 and an EPA release card lands beneath it. A proposal tag begins entering from the lower right.
At 46.2 seconds a closer view shows the proposal tag approaching the delayed program tag. By 46.8 it is attached below the label with a blank lower area.
At 47.0 to 47.6 seconds an empty dashed stamp box forms on the proposal tag. At 47.8 the film returns to the inspector and confirmed footage.
Across 48.0 to 48.8 seconds the inspector raises the stylus to the existing green confirmation on the circled valve image. A small yard view appears above the monitor.
At 49.0 to 49.6 seconds the stylus withdraws below the valve while the green check persists. By 49.8 the room is shown at a medium scale.
At 50.0–50.8 the inspector leans toward the monitor on the left while an empty dashed box labeled AI progressively appears on the right.
The green confirmation and empty AI box remain on the monitor as the view widens to include the desk and yellow hard hat.
At 52.0–52.8 the seated inspector points toward the confirmed plume beside the empty AI box; the closing caption stays below.
The wide inspector room holds through 53.8 with confirmation and empty AI box visible; the caption is gone in the last sample.
All five 54-second samples retain the inspector pointing at the monitor, its green confirmation and empty dashed AI box.
At 55.0–55.8 the wide inspector room continues holding the confirmed plume alongside the empty dashed AI box.
The inspector tableau ends between 56.2 and 56.4, replaced by a dark credits card with the Docket name, website and four source lines.
The dark credits card holds with the flag, Docket title, site address, source lines and authored illustration disclosure.
Across 58.0–58.8 the website and source card remain fixed, including the month-only DroneLife credit.
At 59.0–59.8 the same dark credits retain the Docket title, website, four sources and illustration disclosure.
The final source card remains visible throughout the 60-second samples with no new objects or caption changes.
The three final samples at 61.0, 61.2 and 61.3 retain the same complete credits card.
The opening depicts an illustrated industrial pad and closed drone station, whose two hood leaves begin separating at 0.8.
The opening hood exposes a pale quadcopter resting within the station; the pad equipment remains behind.
Two Texas-outline cards appear above the pad as the drone begins lifting out of its open station at 2.8.
The drone climbs above the station toward the right, with an oval shadow shifting across the pad beneath it.
The hovering drone remains above the equipment while the larger Texas card gains a Permian Basin label by 4.8.
The larger Texas card draws a dotted connection from the Permian Basin pin to an Austin pin while the drone stays airborne.
The airborne drone cuts to a dark desk monitor, with a company-attribution tag resting beside a pen and yellow hard hat.
The screen reveals a survey map and three status rows before a blue flag emerges between the link and pressure rows.
The blue AI alert flag is readable in the right status panel while the company-attribution tag remains on the desk.
The closer monitor view retains the blue alert and desk attribution, with the anomalies caption beneath.
The company tag lifts from the desk and moves beside the screen's blue AI alert, linking the attribution to that flag.
At 11.0–11.8 the attribution tag hangs beside the monitor's blue flag while the survey route remains on the left.
A seated inspector appears left of an angled approval letter with a drone diagram, while a brown stamp enters above.
The stamp contacts the letter's upper date area; the 13.6 close view shows the Air Max and screening labels beneath it.
The lifted stamp reveals the amber date on the letter before the date caption ends; a smaller second stamp descends at right.
The close letter fills the upper frame while a partial inspector and raised stylus remain at lower left; the stamp covers the approval space.
The stamp's departure exposes an amber check and Approved impression at 16.0, during the approval caption.
The Air Max label, generic drone diagram and approval impression persist together as the system-name caption begins.
The system name gains an amber highlight and dark underline while its record-name and generic-drone qualifiers stay below.
At 19.0–19.8 the letter retains the highlighted Air Max name, drone diagram, date and separate approval impression.
An amber underline and highlight build beneath the screening label while approval and Air Max remain visible nearby.
The completed approval letter holds until 21.6, then a seated inspector faces a wall display showing the illustrated drone pad.
The room view places the small drone inside a wall display above the seated inspector; faint route circles appear to its right.
The inspector leans forward below a wall display containing the small drone and pale route; the camera caption continues below.
The 24.2 close view reveals the drone's underslung camera and dashed route, then the drone moves right along the circles.
The drone enters a bright route ring, then the view cuts to its wall-display feed with an infrared inset beginning inside the ring.
The inset expands to show an amber plume above a valve, overlapping the drone feed while the inspector remains cropped at lower left.
The inspector faces a dark review display as a valve-and-plume footage window fades in from the right.
The loaded valve plume stays on the monitor while the seated inspector leans forward and holds the stylus near its lower edge.
The inspector holds beside the loaded footage, then raises the connected stylus arm toward the plume image at 29.8.
In the closer review view the raised stylus follows an arc around the amber plume, leaving a white oval on the monitor.
The oval completes and a green check appears beside the plume where the inspector's finger reaches, then holds through 31.8.
The closer view retains the confirmed plume while a white follow-up inspection tag emerges beside the hand and moves toward the valve inset.
The tag descends onto the valve inset, partly behind the inspector's head and raised forearm, while the monitor's green check holds.
The view cuts to a standing document holder beside the inspector, with a protocol-title block scrolling upward from the page bottom.
The protocol title settles near the document's center, with the inspector seated to its lower left and the explanation caption below.
The close protocol view makes the title readable, with only the AI term marked in amber within the title block.
A white tag descends and settles below the highlighted protocol title, explicitly reading AI appears once, in a title.
At 38.4 a separate program tag and closed calendar replace the protocol page, with an explicit separate-program disclosure above.
The leak-reporting tag lowers and settles in front of the still-closed calendar, with the separate-program caption below.
The cover flips upward to reveal January 22, 2027 above the program tag; the delayed-program caption continues.
The calendar completes its flip and leaves January 22, 2027 fully visible beside the leak-reporting tag.
The closer desk view keeps the January date prominent as an amber bar begins sliding toward the program tag from the left.
The amber Delayed bar settles across the program tag beneath the January 22, 2027 calendar.
The January calendar cuts to a covered rectangular date block; the same delayed program tag remains on the desk.
The cover reveals October 7 and an EPA release card settles beneath it, while a white proposal tag enters at the lower right.
The closer composition shows the future-tense proposal tag attaching below the delayed program, with October 7 and the EPA release above.
An empty dashed stamp space draws on the proposal tag without a completed stamp, then the film returns to the confirmed-plume monitor.
The wide room view shows the inspector's raised stylus touching beside the already-confirmed plume on the review monitor.
The inspector withdraws the stylus from the confirmation, then the view cuts closer while keeping the plume and green check visible.
The closer monitor holds the inspector-confirmed plume on the left while a dashed empty AI box progressively draws on the right.
The tighter closing crop enlarges the confirmation and empty AI box while cutting off the monitor's left edge and much of the inspector.
The enlarged empty AI box holds beside the confirmed plume throughout 52.0–52.8; the closing caption overlaps the cropped inspector.
The enlarged monitor and small exterior inset remain fixed; the closing caption clears by the final 53.8 sample.
The monitor's blank AI area and confirmed plume remain visible across all 54-second samples with the inspector cropped at lower left.
At 55.0–55.8 the same closing crop retains the green confirmation and blank dashed box with no additional on-screen conclusion.
The monitor tableau ends between 56.2 and 56.4, followed by the dark Docket credits and corrected month-only DroneLife source line.
The final dark card retains the Texas flag, Docket title, website, four source lines and authored illustration disclosure.
Across the 58-second samples the credits preserve the month-only DroneLife date and authored-diagram disclosure.
All 59-second samples show the same dark source card with the site address clearly above the smaller credit lines.
The 60.0–60.8 samples preserve the same complete source card without any new transition or text.
The last three samples retain the complete credits card through the 61.3-second final frame sample.
